requirements.name: document-excluded-cases
requirements.text: The corpus in sources/jq.test is byte-for-byte upstream and is never edited. Where a case cannot run under this kit's harness, it is named here instead, so every skip is visible, reasoned, and auditable against the upstream file. This file is a scoring asset: it is hash-verified against the import and restored before grading.

requirements.name: validate-exclusion-entries
requirements.text: One verbatim program line per entry. An entry that matches no case in the corpus is a hard error (exit 2), not a shrug — a silent no-op would quietly re-admit a case the kit cannot run if the corpus pin ever moved.

requirements.name: exclude-module-loader-cases
requirements.text: Only the loader cases are excluded. The module *grammar* cases — `module (.+1); 0`, `module []; 0`, `include "a" (.+1); 0`, `include "a" []; 0`, `include "\ "; 0`, `include "\(a)"; 0`, and `%::wat` — remain in the scored set: they are parse errors that a correct front end rejects without ever touching the filesystem.

requirements.name: executable-json-interface
requirements.text: The deliverable is an executable named jq that reads JSON on stdin.

requirements.name: distinguish-interface-and-conformance-failures
requirements.text: The interface check is separate from the conformance run so that a missing or non-executable program and a genuine conformance failure are distinguishable in the evidence.

requirements.name: score-full-conformance-run
requirements.text: `drydock uat` runs `sh sources/full_test.sh` from the completed application root and takes its exit code and output as the score.

requirements.name: filter-model
requirements.text: A jq program is a "filter": it takes an input, and produces an output.

requirements.name: filter-composition
requirements.text:
Filters can be combined in various ways - you can pipe the output of
one filter into another filter, or collect the output of a filter
into an array.

requirements.name: stream-values
requirements.text:
Some filters produce multiple results, for instance there's one that

requirements.name: numeric-semantics
requirements.text:
Numbers in jq are internally represented by their IEEE754 double
precision approximation.

requirements.name: object-access
requirements.text:
The simplest *useful* filter has the form `.foo`. When given a
JSON object (aka dictionary or hash) as input, `.foo` produces
the value at the key "foo" if the key is present, or null otherwise.

requirements.name: array-access-and-iteration
requirements.text:
When the index value is an integer, `.[<number>]` can index
arrays. Arrays are zero-based, so `.[2]` returns the third
element.

requirements.name: slices
requirements.text:
The `.[<number>:<number>]` syntax can be used to return a
subarray of an array or substring of a string.

The | operator combines two filters by feeding the output(s) of

requirements.text:
The expression 'a == b' will produce 'true' if the results of evaluating
a and b are equal (that is, if they represent equivalent JSON values) and
'false' otherwise.

requirements.text:
The operator `+` takes two filters, applies them both
